When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **0**/10: CALM, no signal aligned vs VIX Spike Tier **3**/4: HIGH, **69%** probability, backwardation and adaptive model both active
Price signals show zero stress while the options market is paying elevated premiums for near-term protection. Trust the VIX detector: backwardation means near-term implied vol is above longer-dated implied vol, and both the adaptive model and the structural term signal are firing together. The crash index is a lagging measure of realized price behavior; the VIX tier is a leading measure of expected behavior. When these two diverge, the options market moves first.
Today's tension
Price sits in complete calm while the options market prices a 69% chance of a vol spike
Bull
The crash index reads zero out of ten with no signals aligned, and the regime is stable. If vol pricing is defensive noise from hedgers, the path for equities is higher.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The dashboard is split down the middle. Price is perfectly calm: the crash index sits at 0 out of 10, no regime shift registers, and the contrarian score at 38 offers no extreme setup in either direction. The options market sees something different. The VIX spike detector is at tier 3 out of 4, the probability of a vol expansion is 69%, and VIX backwardation is active. The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY at 45% confidence, barely a plurality, with a MIXED bias and a regime score of 24. Calm price action is sitting on top of an anxious derivatives market.

For positioning, the gap between price calm and options pricing matters more than either reading alone. Adding long premium directional bets into a 69% vol spike environment means paying rich premiums on both sides. The better posture is reducing gross exposure or using defined-risk structures rather than buying outright protection at elevated vol. The cross-asset divergence picture reinforces that caution: 16 of 43 monitored pairs are registering bearish divergence against only 3 bullish, even while the composite sits in a CALM zone. The mother jaws score at 100 means internal correlation structures are breaking down at the maximum reading.

The reading that changes the stance is resolution of the VIX term structure. If backwardation collapses and realized vol stays muted, the options market was wrong and you can add risk. If price starts catching up to what options have been pricing, the crash index confirms and the bearish divergence picture gets its catalyst. Watch which moves first.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence, in plain terms, means two assets that normally move together have started moving apart (or vice versa) more than their historical relationship would suggest. Correlation drift is the measurable shift in that rolling relationship over time.

The composite zone reads CALM, but 44% of the 43 monitored pairs are diverging, 16 of them in the bearish direction against only 3 bullish. The mother jaws score, which aggregates all that drift into a single composite reading, hits 100: the maximum.

The sharpest split in the current picture is NVDA versus AMD, where correlation drifted from nearly flat at -0.01 to -0.93: these two semis are now moving in strong opposition, a signal of intra-sector rotation rather than a broad group move. SPY versus RSP drifted from -0.06 to +0.65, meaning the cap-weighted index is increasingly decoupling from the equal-weight version: a small number of large stocks are doing the heavy lifting while most others trail.

Copper and gold (HG versus GC) moving from +0.21 to +0.81 in tandem is an unusual joint bid that points toward reflationary positioning rather than a clean risk-on or safe-haven move. The SMH to SPY drift to +0.86 tells you semis are locking in with the index, not driving it independently.

Confluences — most proven alpha of the framework 0/3 ACTIVE
AI read · what the confluences mean now

All three monitored confluences are inactive today. VIX backwardation is firing inside the VIX spike detector, but it has not combined with credit stress (HYG), small-cap drawdown, or yen safe-haven flow to produce any of the joint confirmation signals.

That absence is its own read. The options market is pricing fear, but credit spreads and currency markets have not confirmed the same concern.

When vol and credit diverge like this, credit tends to be the more reliable leading signal for actual price dislocations. A vol spike that stays contained to the options market without credit or FX confirmation is more likely to fade than to accelerate.

The trigger that changes that: if HYG starts widening or the yen moves into a safe-haven bid, the confluence picture shifts fast and the 69% vol probability gets hard confirmation from the asset classes that matter most for positioning.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The five-day cross-region screen shows a clear tech-and-China tilt leading the pack. The Hang Seng leads Asia at +3.7% while Korea's KOSPI sits at -1.4%, a sharp split between China-adjacent liquidity and the more export-cyclical Korean market.

In Europe, Germany's DAX at +2.1% is running ahead of Switzerland's SMI at +0.1%, favoring cyclicals over defensives. The US pattern repeats: NDX at +2.6% leads while RUT at +1.1% lags.

Mega-cap tech and growth are the common thread across all three regions. Crypto breaks from that pattern entirely: SOL at -0.2% and ETH at -2.7% are both down over five days, with ETH the weakest reading on the entire screen.

Risk appetite is concentrated and narrow. The lead-lag implication for the US session is constructive for large-cap tech, but the crypto weakness and small-cap underperformance signal that speculative appetite beyond the top handful of stocks is thin.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 0/10 · CALM — no signal aligned
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The crash index at 0 out of 10 and the VIX spike detector at tier 3 out of 4 are measuring different things, and the gap between them is informative rather than contradictory. The crash index reads price-side signals: drawdown depth, momentum breaks, breadth collapse.

None have triggered today. The VIX detector reads the options market's expectation of future vol: backwardation is active (near-term implied vol is above longer-dated vol, meaning traders are paying up for short-term coverage), and the adaptive model is also confirming.

At 69% probability, the options market is positioned for a vol expansion that has yet to show up in price. This is a coherent state.

Price can sit still while derivatives position for a move, and that gap can persist for several sessions before resolving in either direction. Backwardation is the sharper of the two signals here because it reflects actual money paying elevated premiums for near-term downside coverage, which is a harder signal to fake than a model output.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 0/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
